articles.title: Talk to a remote MCP server with only the Python standard library (and call two tools without a key)
articles.excerpt: Most "connect your agent to MCP" guides start with installing an SDK and a client. But the protocol underneath a remote MCP server is just JSON-RPC over HTTPS POST. If you want to know what a server a…
articles.body: Most "connect your agent to MCP" guides start with installing an SDK and a client. But the protocol underneath a remote MCP server is just JSON-RPC over HTTPS POST. If you want to know what a server actually does before you wire it into Claude, Cursor or VS Code, you can talk to it with the Python standard library in about 60 lines. This post does exactly that against a real server, https://siftwright.com/mcp . Two of its nine tools, domain_whois and pqc_scan , answer without an API key (one domain per call, with a free daily limit per network). That means every command below works as you read it. I ran all of them on 26 November 2026, and the outputs shown are from those runs.

articles.excerpt: Murmury is an open-source call copilot for Mac. During a Zoom, Meet or Teams call it transcribes the other side on your Mac with Whisper, notices when someone asks you something, and shows a short ans…
articles.body: Murmury is an open-source call copilot for Mac. During a Zoom, Meet or Teams call it transcribes the other side on your Mac with Whisper, notices when someone asks you something, and shows a short answer from your own documents (a PDF, a spreadsheet, your notes) in a small window that screen sharing doesn't capture. It's Python and PySide6, GPL-3.0. In its first month, 30 people have contributed and 44 pull requests have been merged, many of them first pull requests ever. This post is for the next ones. Why most issues don't need a Mac The app itself runs on macOS, but most of the code is plain Python: loading documents, building the prompt, choosing models, parsing answers, the setup screen's logic.

articles.title: Check a UAE WPS salary file (SIF) in Python before the bank rejects it
articles.excerpt: Private-sector salaries in the UAE are paid through the Wage Protection System (WPS), which runs at the Central Bank of the UAE. Each payroll run starts with a Salary Information File (SIF), a small t…
articles.body: Private-sector salaries in the UAE are paid through the Wage Protection System (WPS), which runs at the Central Bank of the UAE. Each payroll run starts with a Salary Information File (SIF), a small text file that the employer uploads to its bank or exchange house. The bank checks the file before anyone is paid. Some mistakes, such as an invalid routing code or a wrong IBAN, get the whole file rejected, and Mashreq's guide says that rejection can take up to two working days to come back. Meanwhile, every employee in the file is waiting for their salary. This post explains the format and gives you a Python script, using only the standard library, that catches the common mistakes before you upload. The format in brief A SIF is plain text with comma-separated fields and no header row.
articles.author: Monu Kumar

articles.title: Enclawed Code: How Deterministic Security Layers Harden Claude Code Agent Execution
articles.excerpt: Enclawed Code wraps Claude Code in a deterministic security layer that checks every action before execution. The core insight: stop asking the LLM to judge safety. Instead, enforce boundaries at the i…
articles.body: Enclawed Code wraps Claude Code in a deterministic security layer that checks every action before execution. The core insight: stop asking the LLM to judge safety. Instead, enforce boundaries at the infrastructure layer using a fixed rule that asks one question: can this action be undone? The project ships as open source with a companion research paper showing zero harmful actions passed and zero harmless actions blocked across 15,021 real tool calls. It also claims 7.7x fewer approval prompts than Claude Code's default permission mode. The Problem with Probabilistic Guardrails Claude Code and similar agents execute shell commands, edit files, and call tools on your local machine. They read context along the way: README files, web pages, tool output.

articles.excerpt: The Aladdin sequel The Return of Jafar is often derided as a bad, cheap sequel which started Disney's direct-to-video sequel trend, but I love it
articles.body: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

articles.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
articles.excerpt: Seven years later, a first watch of Tom Hooper’s Cats on Netflix finds plenty to enjoy, especially Taylor Swift’s catnip number.
articles.body: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
